title: A Cue Without Looking Down
author: Agile Lens
source: Original text created for the Understudy sample pack, October 28, 2026. Not a quotation or a device-readiness claim.

entries.text: Original rehearsal text. Pause and resume at your own pace.
I am going to read a short scene while keeping my eyes up. The phone controls the script. The glasses show the words.
First I will use the single-line view. Watch the cue change as I move through the text. A long cue is divided into smaller pages.
Now I will switch to the flowing view. The active words are cyan. Earlier words dim, and the next words stay white.
I can pause here. Nothing should keep moving while I explain what you are seeing.
I can change the speed, resume, or drag back to a place I want to rehearse. Those controls stay on the phone.
This is a rehearsal aid. If I lose the connection, I will check it and reopen the glasses display from the phone.
The useful test is simple: can I keep the thought, find the next line, and keep looking at the person in front of me?
